correctness.rationale: For any h>=2, the polynomial-base integers B_j have unique unordered pair sums, since their linear coefficient exceeds every possible difference of two quadratic sums. Quotient-remainder decoding modulo R makes all distinct-index E_a+E_b unique, hence all weight products are unique; antipodal weight intervals are disjoint. The two Fourier power spectra invert to exact autocorrelations. Nonantipodal lags identify the physical pair by product code; two different zero-lag weights determine both magnitudes and a nonzero directional correlation determines relative phase. Antipodal lags produce independent real and imaginary components by a pi/2 mask phase, while zero-lag ratio uniquely selects the antipodal pair. Zero and singleton cases are handled; one mask fails even on nonzero singleton pairs. Checker recorded 145789 exact finite pair-code comparisons and 1660 decoder tests, but the symbolic proof carries the infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The exact optimal two-mask assertion on all even cyclic lengths, using one flat and one nonreal bounded-amplitude two-phase mask, is not implied by the closest odd-cycle two-real-mask result, by the earlier three-mask even-cycle construction, or by random/full-signal/oversampled phase-retrieval guarantees. Real-mask antipodal impossibility cannot be applied to a complex quadrature mask. Targeted searches and full primary text of the most directly comparable odd-cycle result found no equivalent; two full-text gaps leave a nonzero historical equivalence risk.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed exact complex two-mask construction for even cyclic two-sparse signals may exist under different terminology (coded diffraction, sparse autocorrelation, complex Sidon masks).

No quantitative noise-uniform recovery guarantee is established.

value.rationale: The minimum number of full coded diffraction patterns is a canonical signal-design quantity. The theorem closes the even/odd parity gap for arbitrary two-sparse complex cyclic signals, proves the optimum of two masks for all even sizes, uses only a flat plus a bounded-contrast two-quadrature-phase mask, and supplies an exact algorithm. The Sidon-type amplitude code separates all nonantipodal supports while independent imaginary-phase information resolves the previously decisive antipodal obstruction. The claim is not a routine restatement of a three-mask result and makes no unsupported full-signal or noise-uniform promise.
